q-124885.name: Question 1
q-124885.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}x{y}^{2}\,dx+\frac{1}{x}\,dy,$ where $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=\frac{1}{t}\,i+t\,j$ for $t\in [1,3]?$
q-124885.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{t},\,y(t)=t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}x{y}^{2}\,dx+\frac{1}{x}\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{3}x{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+\frac{1}{x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}(x{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{1}{x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{t}\cdot {t}^{2}\cdot (-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})+\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{t})}\cdot 1\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}-\frac{1}{t}+t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cxy2dx+1xdy, where C is parametrized by r(t)=1ti+tj for t∈[1,3]?

a
∫13t−1tdt
b
∫132tdt
c
2∫131tdt
d
∫13t2−1tdt
e
∫13t2+1tdt
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=1t,y(t)=t.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(1t)i+ddt(t)j=−1t2i+j.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫Cxy2dx+1xdy=∫13xy2dxdtdt+1xdydtdt=∫13(xy2dxdt+1xdydt)dt=∫131t⋅t2⋅(−1t2)+1(1t)⋅1dt=∫13−1t+tdt=∫13t2−1tdt

q-124870.name: Question 2
q-124870.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}x\,dx+({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,dy,$ where $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\,i+j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ]?$
q-124870.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,y(t)=1.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}x\,dx+({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+({sin}^{2}⁡(2t)-{1}^{2})\cdot 0\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

q-124870.html:
Question 2
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cxdx+(x2−y2)dy, where C is parametrized by r(t)=sin⁡(2t)i+j for t∈[0,2π]?

a
∫02π2sin⁡(4t)dt
b
∫02πsin⁡(4t)dt
c
∫02πsin2⁡(2t)+sin⁡(2t)−1dt
d
∫02πsin⁡(4t)−cos2⁡(2t)dt
e
∫02πsin⁡(2t)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=sin⁡(2t),y(t)=1.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(sin⁡(2t))i+ddt(1)j=2cos⁡(2t)i.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫Cxdx+(x2−y2)dy=∫02πxdxdtdt+(x2−y2)dydtdt=∫02π(xdxdt+(x2−y2)dydt)dt=∫02πsin⁡(2t)⋅2cos⁡(2t)+(sin2⁡(2t)−12)⋅0dt=∫02π2sin⁡(2t)cos⁡(2t)dt=∫02πsin⁡(4t)dt

q-124877.name: Question 3
q-124877.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy,$ where $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,\pi ]?$
q-124877.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }-{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cydx+xdy, where C is parametrized by r(t)=cos⁡ti+sin⁡tj for t∈[0,π]?

a
∫0πcos⁡tdt
b
∫0πcos⁡t−sin⁡tdt
c
∫0πcos⁡(2t)dt
d
∫0πdt
e
2∫0πcos⁡(2t)dt
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=cos⁡t,y(t)=sin⁡t.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(cos⁡t)i+ddt(sin⁡t)j=−sin⁡ti+cos⁡tj.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫Cydx+xdy=∫0πydxdtdt+xdydtdt=∫0π(xdxdt+ydydt)dt=∫0πsin⁡t⋅(−sin⁡t)+cos⁡t⋅cos⁡tdt=∫0π−sin2⁡t+cos2⁡tdt=∫0πcos⁡(2t)dt

q-124875.name: Question 4
q-124875.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+(x+2)\,dy,$ where $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=(t-2)\,i+({t}^{3}-t)\,j$ for $t\in [1,2]?$
q-124875.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t-2,\,y(t)={t}^{3}-t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-t)\,j \\  & =i+(3{t}^{2}-1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+(x+2)\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(x+y)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+(x+2)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}((x+y)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+(x+2)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(t-2+{t}^{3}-t)\cdot 1+(t-2+2)\cdot (3{t}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{t}^{3}-2+3{t}^{3}-t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}4{t}^{3}-t-2\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

q-124878.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}(x-y)\,dx+(y-x)\,dy,$ where $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}]?$
q-124878.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y(t)=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(x-y)\,dx+(y-x)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(x-y)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+(y-x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}((x-y)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+(y-x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t))\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-4{sin}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}4({cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

q-124832.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix $r(t)=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+t\,k$ for $t\in [\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{\pi }{3}]?$
q-124832.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)=t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}(-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+t\cdot 1\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}t+2{sin}^{2}⁡t+2{cos}^{2}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}t+2\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫C−ydx+xdy+zdz, where C is a portion of the helix r(t)=2cos⁡ti+2sin⁡tj+tk for t∈[π4,π3]?

a
∫π/4π/3t2−sin⁡tdt
b
∫π/4π/3t2+9dt
c
∫π/4π/3t2+cos2⁡tdt
d
∫π/4π/3t+2dt
e
∫π/4π/3t+2cos⁡2tdt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=2cos⁡t,y(t)=2sin⁡t,z(t)=t.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj+dzdtk=ddt(2cos⁡t)i+ddt(2sin⁡t)j+ddt(t)k=−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tj+k.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫C−ydx+xdy+zdz=∫π/4π/3−ydxdtdt+xdydtdt+zdzdtdt=∫π/4π/3(−ydxdt+xdydt+zdzdt)dt=∫π/4π/3−2sin⁡t⋅(−2sin⁡t)+2cos⁡t⋅(2cos⁡t)+t⋅1dt=∫π/4π/3t+2sin2⁡t+2cos2⁡tdt=∫π/4π/3t+2dt

q-124809.name: Question 7
q-124809.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}{x}^{3}\,dx+z\,dy+y\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix $r(t)=t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k$ for $t\in [0,\pi ]?$
q-124809.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,z(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,k \\  & =\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}{x}^{3}\,dx+z\,dy+y\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{x}^{3}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+y\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }({x}^{3}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+y\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{t}^{3}\cdot (1)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{t}^{3}+{cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{t}^{3}+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cx3dx+zdy+ydz, where C is a portion of the helix r(t)=ti+cos⁡tj+sin⁡tk for t∈[0,π]?

a
∫0πcos3⁡tdt
b
∫0πt3+cos⁡2tdt
c
∫0πcos2⁡t+1dt
d
∫0πt2−cos⁡tdt
e
∫0πcos⁡2t+sin⁡tdt
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=t,y(t)=cos⁡t,z(t)=sin⁡t.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj+dzdtk=ddt(t)i+ddt(cos⁡t)j+ddt(sin⁡t)k=i−sin⁡tj+cos⁡tk.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫Cx3dx+zdy+ydz=∫0πx3dxdtdt+zdydtdt+ydzdtdt=∫0π(x3dxdt+zdydt+ydzdt)dt=∫0πt3⋅(1)+sin⁡t⋅(−sin⁡t)+cos⁡t⋅(cos⁡t)dt=∫0πt3+cos2⁡t−sin2⁡tdt=∫0πt3+cos⁡2tdt

q-124837.name: Question 8
q-124837.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+{e}^{t}\,k$ for $t\in [\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ]?$
q-124837.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=5\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)={e}^{t}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,k \\  & =-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+{e}^{t}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }25{cos}^{2}⁡t-25{sin}^{2}⁡t+{e}^{2t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }25\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+{e}^{2t}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cydx+xdy+zdz, where C is a portion of the curve r(t)=5cos⁡ti+5sin⁡tj+etk for t∈[π2,π]?

a
∫π/2π5sin⁡2t+e2tdt
b
∫π/2π25sin⁡2t+etdt
c
∫π/2π25cos⁡2t+e2tdt
d
∫π/2π5cos⁡t+e2tdt
e
∫π/2π5cos⁡2t+etdt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=5cos⁡t,y(t)=5sin⁡t,z(t)=et.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj+dzdtk=ddt(5cos⁡t)i+ddt(5sin⁡t)j+ddt(et)k=−5sin⁡ti+5cos⁡tj+etk.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫Cydx+xdy+zdz=∫π/2πydxdtdt+xdydtdt+zdzdtdt=∫π/2π(ydxdt+xdydt+zdzdt)dt=∫π/2π5sin⁡t⋅(−5sin⁡t)+5cos⁡t⋅(5cos⁡t)+et⋅etdt=∫π/2π25cos2⁡t−25sin2⁡t+e2tdt=∫π/2π25cos⁡2t+e2tdt

q-124866.name: Question 9
q-124866.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}xy\,dx+yz\,dy+z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the line $r(t)=t\,i+5t\,j+\,k$ for $t\in [2,3]?$
q-124866.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)=5t,\,z(t)=1.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\,k \\  & =\,i+5\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xy\,dx+yz\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{2}^{3}xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+yz\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}(xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+yz\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}5{t}^{2}\cdot (1)+5t\cdot (5)+1\cdot (0)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}5{t}^{2}+25t\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cxydx+yzdy+zdz, where C is a portion of the line r(t)=ti+5tj+k for t∈[2,3]?

a
∫23t3+20tdt
b
∫233t2+13dt
c
∫235t2+25tdt
d
∫23t+12dt
e
∫23t4−4dt
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=t,y(t)=5t,z(t)=1.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj+dzdtk=ddt(t)i+ddt(5t)j+ddt(1)k=i+5j.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫Cxydx+yzdy+zdz=∫23xydxdtdt+yzdydtdt+zdzdtdt=∫23(xydxdt+yzdydt+zdzdt)dt=∫235t2⋅(1)+5t⋅(5)+1⋅(0)dt=∫235t2+25tdt

q-124830.name: Question 10
q-124830.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy+{z}^{2}\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+{t}^{2}\,k$ for $t\in [0,\frac{3\pi }{2}]?$
q-124830.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)={t}^{2}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,k \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy+{z}^{2}\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+{z}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}(-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+{z}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+{t}^{4}\cdot (2t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}2{t}^{5}-4{sin}^{2}⁡t-4{cos}^{2}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}2{t}^{5}-4\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫C−ydx+xdy+z2dz, where C is a portion of the curve r(t)=2cos⁡ti−2sin⁡tj+t2k for t∈[0,3π2]?

a
∫03π/22t3+2dt
b
∫03π/22t4−2sin2⁡tdt
c

∫03π/22t5−4dt
e
∫03π/22t4−2cos⁡tdt

Along the curve, we have x(t)=2cos⁡t,y(t)=−2sin⁡t,z(t)=t2.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj+dzdtk=ddt(2cos⁡t)i+ddt(−2sin⁡t)j+ddt(t2)k=−2sin⁡ti−2cos⁡tj+2tk.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫C−ydx+xdy+z2dz=∫03π/2−ydxdtdt+xdydtdt+z2dzdtdt=∫03π/2(−ydxdt+xdydt+z2dzdt)dt=∫03π/22sin⁡t⋅(−2sin⁡t)+2cos⁡t⋅(−2cos⁡t)+t4⋅(2t)dt=∫03π/22t5−4sin2⁡t−4cos2⁡tdt=∫03π/22t5−4dt

q-81170.name: Question 11
q-81170.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}\frac{x}{y}\,dx+\frac{y}{x}\,dy,$ where $C$ is a portion of the ellipse $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].$
q-81170.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\frac{x}{y}\,dx+\frac{y}{x}\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{x}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+\frac{y}{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\frac{x}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{y}{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{2}-0]-[0-4] \\  & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-124712.name: Question 12
q-124712.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}x\,dx-z\,dy+y\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=3{t}^{2}\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ].$
q-124712.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=3{t}^{2},\,y(t)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,k \\  & =6t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}x\,dx-z\,dy+y\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt-z\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+y\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-z\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+y\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }3{t}^{2}\cdot (6t)-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }18{t}^{3}-9{cos}^{2}⁡t-9{sin}^{2}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }18{t}^{3}-9\,dt \\  & =(\frac{9{t}^{4}}{2}-9t){|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =72{\pi }^{4}-18\pi \end{aligned}
$$

q-90723.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}(3x+y)\,dx+x\,dy,$ where $C$ is a portion of the parabola parametrized by $r(t)={t}^{2}\,i+(4t-1)\,j$ for $t\in [0,2].$
q-90723.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)={t}^{2},\,y(t)=4t-1.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1)\,j \\  & =2t\,i+4\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(3x+y)\,dx+x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3x+y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}((3x+y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3{t}^{2}+4t-1)\cdot 2t+{t}^{2}\cdot 4\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}6{t}^{3}+8{t}^{2}-2t+4{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}6{t}^{3}+12{t}^{2}-2t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4}+4{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =[\frac{3}{2}(2)^{4}+4(2)^{3}-{2}^{2}]-[0] \\  & =[24+32-4] \\  & =52\end{aligned}

q-90840.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}-\frac{1}{y}\,dx+\frac{y}{x}\,dy+dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix parametrized by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+t\,k$ for $t\in [0,\pi ].$

Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)=t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-\frac{1}{y}\,dx+\frac{y}{x}\,dy+dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{1}{y}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+\frac{y}{x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(-\frac{1}{y}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{y}{x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+1\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }2+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =(2t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(2\pi -\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\  & =2(\pi +1)\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
